messages:
ellie (Sales): FYI Solstice wants to POC a customer-supplied gguf q4_k_m variant of llama-3-13b for document summarization. They want: compatibility check, pricing for a 3-month Dedicated POC, security questionnaire answers, and an ETA to certify the variant into our catalog. Kickoff Mon morning.

ravi (SE): Quick checklist: 1) Is the gguf format with q4_k_m quant supported by our runtime? 2) Any required adapter for KV cache / streaming? 3) Memory footprint and recommended batch size for a 4096 seq?

nora (Security): Also need model provenance details from Solstice, licensing, fingerprint/hash, and whether the weights contain third-party licensed components. We'll need answers for the security questionnaire before private deployment.

thomas (Infra): From infra side we need the model file and a sample inference trace (1-2 requests) to run our variant validator. If it passes, we can promote to a staged catalog entry. Approx run: a small perf job on a single GPU node.

ellie (Sales): Solstice says they can provide the gguf file + license statement. They asked if we can do the first compatibility pass in 48 hours. Is that feasible?

ravi (SE): 48h reasonable if we get the file and a small prompt corpus. I can run local variant compat and KV cache smoke tests. Typical commands I use:
```
# import to test cluster (dev only)
redwood model import --name solstice-llama3-q4 --format gguf --file /tmp/model.gguf --quant q4_k_m
# quick perf run
redwood infer --model solstice-llama3-q4 --prompt-file sample_prompts.json --max-tokens 256 --batch 1
```
I'll share exact memory/latency numbers.

li (Acct Exec): Pricing ask: Solstice is a mid-market customer and wants a 3-month Dedicated POC with predictable throughput. Ballpark: for a 1-GPU reserved node with burst capacity and 99th p50 latency SLO, our POC pricing typically starts at $8k/mo for baseline and +$X per peak vGPU. We should fine-tune after we know batch/seq costs.

nora (Security): One heads-up: if customers upload custom weights we require a signed checksum and an export control attestation. Also for Private deployments we need to ensure KMS integration is set up before onboarding.

ravi (SE): On compatibility specifics: q4_k_m can have slightly different kernel paths; runtime supports q4 types but we must validate KV cache alignment (we use contiguous KV layout). If the model uses a nonstandard tokenizer or special BOS/EOS tokens we need a mapping.

thomas (Infra): For the variant validator we'll run: model hash check, checksum, basic tokenization test, single-token autoregressive step, KV cache correctness (prefix match), and end-to-end perf. Expect 4-6 hours compute once file is ingested. If issues show up, debugging might take longer.

ellie (Sales): Great — action items: 1) Solstice to upload model + license + sample prompts 2) Ravi to run compat tests 3) Nora to prep required answers for the security questionnaire 4) Thomas to schedule validator job 5) Li to draft POC pricing estimate and payment terms.

ops-bot: Reminder: create POC ticket #POC-5879 and attach uploaded artifacts.

ravi (SE): If we want to fast-track cert into catalog for hosted customers, we need to run the quantized regression suite (quality checks) against our golden prompts. That takes ~1 day. For Dedicated-only POC we can skip catalog cert initially.

ellie (Sales): Solstice prefers hosted-like behavior (streaming + function calls) but they are okay to start on Dedicated. Can we emulate streaming during POC?

ravi (SE): Yes, streaming works if the runtime has compatible chunky output. We'll enable chunked output; KV cache works the same. I'll include a sample curl stream snippet in the results.

nora (Security): I'll post the minimal questionnaire answers we can provide quickly and flag anything that needs Legal.

li (Acct Exec): I will draft a 90-day POC proposal: base fee $22k for 3 months (Dedicated node + support + 2 FTE eng hours for onboarding) with optional addons for increased concurrency. Will circulate after Ravi's perf numbers.

ellie (Sales): Perfect. Solstice target: start ingest by Mon 09:00 PT. I'll request upload link today and ask for the license & provenance doc.

ravi (SE): Ok I'll be on standby Mon morning for the import and run tests. If anyone wants the perf table format I'll post it as CSV.

thomas (Infra): Scheduled a 2-hour slot Mon 11:00 PT for validator cluster. Ops will post node details to POC-5879.

nora (Security): I'll upload the partial questionnaire answers to the ticket and highlight Legal blockers (if any).

ellie (Sales): Thanks team. Solstice asked one more question: can we support traceroute of user tokens for debug during POC without retaining PII? Answer?

ravi (SE): We can surface per-request traces with masked user identifiers. We never store raw user tokens in logs; we hash/nonce them for traces. Nora confirm?

nora (Security): Confirmed. We'll provide masked traces and keep retention per our policy. Any requests for raw tokens will require a signed attestation and Legal approval.

ellie (Sales): Great — I'll message Solstice with the plan and timeline. I'll attach this thread to the ticket.

ops-bot: Ticket #POC-5879 created and linked to channel.
